messages:
maria: Heads-up — after pushing the new base-image nvidia-toolkit:2.4.0 to the gpu-nodepool us-west2-gpu-2 this morning, ~18% of GPU pods fail at container start with libcuda/libnvidia-ml mount errors. Minimal traffic impact so far but batch jobs are queuing.

sam: ugh. can you paste the error logs?

maria: here's one from a failed pod: ```Warning  FailedMount  2s (x3 over 10s)  kubelet  MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "nvidia-bin": mount failed: exit status 1
error: nvidia-container-cli: initialization error: device not found: no such file or directory
failed to stat /var/lib/nvidia/driver/libnvidia-ml.so.1: no such file or directory
```

jin: same errors reported by the ML batch queue. which nodes were upgraded?

maria: only us-west2-gpu-2 nodes got the new base-image yesterday (image tag: rdx-gpu-base:2026-03-12). rolling upgrade started 06:00 UTC.

carla: ops-bot shows 7 nodes rebooted and kubelet restarted during the upgrade. @ops-bot can you confirm which kernel and nvidia driver versions are on those nodes?

ops-bot: Replied to thread. Upgraded nodes (7): kernel 5.15.0-1033, nvidia-driver 535.98, nvidia-container-toolkit 2.4.0, libnvidia 535.98. Previous pool had nvidia-container-toolkit 2.3.1 + driver 525.x.

sam: looks like the toolkit 2.4.0 changed the expected lib path/uid mapping for the driver bind mounts. we've seen a similar UID/GID mismatch in an internal repro last quarter.

sre-anna: quick mitigation: cordon the remaining not-yet-upgraded nodes in the pool and drain one upgraded node for deeper debugging. we should also pin rollout to rdx-gpu-base:2026-03-01 for the rest of the pool.

maria: pinning sounds good. rolling upgrade paused. I'm reverting one node to old base-image to test.

eng-mike: when you revert, please capture `ls -la /var/lib/nvidia/driver` and `cat /etc/nvidia-container-runtime/host-files-for-container.d/*` from both a good and bad node. differences there will confirm mount path changes.

maria: repro logs attached (pasted inline): ```# bad node
$ ls -la /var/lib/nvidia/driver
ls: cannot access '/var/lib/nvidia/driver': No such file or directory
# good node
$ ls -la /var/lib/nvidia/driver
-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 213K Mar 12 06:12 libnvidia-ml.so.1
-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 5.1M Mar 12 06:12 libcuda.so.1
```

jin: interesting — missing host side dir on the bad nodes. maybe the toolkit init scripts expect a different driver install path or the base image removed the stub files.

carla: any chance systemd service ordering changed so nvidia modules load after nvidia-container-toolkit attempts to create mounts?

sam: plausible. 2.4.0 added a container-side check that fails fast if host files are missing. previous version tolerated missing host stubs.

maria: I'm planning a controlled rollback of the 7 upgraded nodes to the previous image (rdx-gpu-base:2026-03-01) and re-run the upgrade in a test pool with additional checks. will also open a toolkit issue.

deploy-bot: Deployment action queued: rollback image for nodes [us-west2-gpu-2-node-1 .. node-7] -> rdx-gpu-base:2026-03-01. ETA 12m.

sre-anna: also create a short preflight: verify existence of /var/lib/nvidia/driver and `nvidia-smi` before marking node upgraded. add into upgrade job.

maria: done, added a preflight and a healthcheck step. rolling rollback started.

eng-mike: for follow-up, we should add a post-upgrade e2e that launches a tiny gpu job that mounts /usr/local/nvidia and runs `nvidia-smi` to catch this early.

sam: +1. we should also check region capacity fallback plan — if we need to evacuate workloads while nodes are pinned, us-east-1 only has ~40% spare GPUs atm.

jin: flagged to support — I'll coordinate cross-region job scheduling if rollback doesn't clear the queue within 30m.

carla: filing a short incident note in the incident channel with the root cause hypothesis (toolkit 2.4.0 expecting host driver files that some images don't include) and the mitigation steps. :memo:
